contexts.text: I once heard the Angels speaking with Newton about a vacuum... Newton said that he knows that the Divine which Is infills all things; and that he himself shudders at the idea of nothing as concerning a vacuum, because that idea is destructive of all things. He exhorts those who speak with him concerning a vacuum to beware of the idea of nothing, calling it a swoon...

Concerning Newton. - I have sometimes spoken with him. He is a very sincere man, and is among his own, and is loved. He said to me that he now knows that the Lord is the Sun of the angelic Heaven, and that all light is from Him, which in its essence is Divine intelligence... He had Known also that there was one life, which causes anyone to live, and that this life appears with them as light... (Continued. See Colour.)
Concerning Newton. - I have spoken with Newton concerning a vacuum, and concerning colours.
Concerning a vacuum, he said that in the world he had believed in the existence of a vacuum. (Continued. See Vacuum.)
Concerning colours, he said... (Continued. See Colour.)
These are Newton's own words, which he wants me to communicate.
In the suburb (of London) to the left dwell many of their learned, and, with them, Newton. They descend thither by a way sloping downwards.
